title: Longest run of ones after one deletion
description:
A list holds only zeros and ones. You must delete exactly one element from it, and then you want the longest stretch of consecutive ones that is left.

Implement a function called LongestOnesAfterDeletion that receives a list of integers, each of them 0 or 1, and returns the length of the longest stretch made only of ones that the list can have once one element has been deleted.

LongestOnesAfterDeletion([1, 1, 0, 1]) -> 3. Deleting the zero joins the two runs of ones.
LongestOnesAfterDeletion([0, 1, 1, 1, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1]) -> 5. Deleting the zero at position 4 joins three ones and two ones.

The deletion is not optional. When the list has no zero, one of the ones still has to go: LongestOnesAfterDeletion([1, 1, 1]) -> 2. When the list has no one at all, nothing is left to count: LongestOnesAfterDeletion([0, 0, 0]) -> 0.

The hidden tests also check a list of a single element, two zeros next to each other (which no single deletion can bridge), a zero at the very start of the list, and a best stretch that comes after an earlier, shorter one.
objective: Find the longest run of ones a binary list can have after deleting exactly one element.

metadata.source: Longest Subarray of 1's After Deleting One Element, LeetCode 1493 (https://leetcode.com/problems/longest-subarray-of-1s-after-deleting-one-element/description/)

title: Longest substring with no repeated character
description:
A substring is a run of consecutive characters taken from a string. Some substrings use every character at most once.

Implement a function called LongestUniqueSubstring that receives a string and returns the length, in characters, of its longest substring in which no character appears twice.

LongestUniqueSubstring("abcabcbb") -> 3, from "abc".
LongestUniqueSubstring("bbbbb") -> 1, from "b".
LongestUniqueSubstring("pwwkew") -> 3, from "wke". The answer has to be a substring: "pwke" is not one, because its letters are not next to each other.
LongestUniqueSubstring("") -> 0.

The string can hold any character at all, not only letters: spaces, digits, symbols, accented letters and characters from other writing systems. Length is counted in characters, not in bytes: LongestUniqueSubstring("héllo wörld") -> 7, from "o wörld".

The hidden tests also check a string with no repeats at all, and strings such as "abba" -> 2 and "dvdf" -> 3.
objective: Find the length of the longest substring of a string in which no character repeats.

metadata.source: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters, LeetCode 3 (https://leetcode.com/problems/longest-substring-without-repeating-characters/description/)
